State of Maine
DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION
Testimony of Beth Lambert, Chief Teaching and Learning Officer
In Support of: L.D. 74
An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Sponsored by: Representative Brennan
F ebiuary 27, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Beth Lambert, and I am here today representing the Department speaking in support
of L.D. 74, An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline.
We have heard clearly that schools are facing significant demands, and many educators and
administrators need more time to fully implement the revisions from the last standards review.
Maine's state education standards, the Maine Learning Results, serve as guideposts that define what knowledge, and skills students must achieve to be prepared for school, work, and life after high school graduation. As required by statute, the Department reviews these standards on a fiveyear rotating cycle, beginning with a review of the social studies and science content standards and continuing through the following content areas: English language arts; mathematics; life and career readiness; visual and performing arts; health, physical education, and wellness; and world languages. The Department has paused this review on occasion, in cases of unusual
circumstances, such as the pandemic.
During the most recent cycle, which began in 2023, the Department received extensive feedback from educators and administrators that the current five-year cycle is too short, placing undue burden on SAUs. Specifically, educators noted that there is insufficient time to fully implement
revisions, support staff in adapting to changes, and assess the impact before the new review begins. Extending the timeline will provide SAUs with the necessary time to align curricula, support, and evaluate changes before new revisions take place.
If enacted, L.D. 74 would extend the review cycle from five to seven years, ensuring a more
sustainable and effective implementation process. This adjustment requires no changes to existing rule language and has no associated costs.
This proposal reflects our commitment to responding to the realities schools face and supporting
educators and students in meaningful, sustainable Ways. By allowing for greater stability and focus in classrooms, we believe this change will strengthen education across Maine.
1

For these reasons, the Department of Education is in support of L.D. 74 An Act to Update the
System of Learning Results Review Timeline that Was recommended by teachers in schools and
districts that you represent. I would be happy to answer any questions the Committee may have, and I will be available for work sessions on this bill.

Testimony of Debra Mclntyre, Executive Director, on behalf of the members of the Maine Curriculum Leaders Association, testifying in support of LD 74 An Act to Update the
System of Learning Results Review Timeline.
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs
Committee, my name is Debra Mclntyre, and l am the Executive Director of the Maine Curriculum Leaders Association. On behalf of the members of MCLA, l am testifying in support
of LD 74 An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline.
The current review cycle of the Maine Learning Results of 5 years, is limiting and problematic
for school districts across the state. While we recognize the value and importance of reviewing
the state standards in a timely fashion, for a truly impactful implementation process more time is
'
needed for school districts to make necessary adjustments to curriculum, instruction and assessment that incorporates revised standards.
As the Maine Learning Results guides the work of educators in all content areas, it is essential that there is adequate time for school districts to review any changes and to plan revisions to local curriculum. ln addition, some revisions require support for implementation including professional development and providing for adequate resources. The additional time would
allow both the MDOE and school districts to plan for a successful implementation.
For these reasons MCLA supports LD 74. Thank you for your time.

TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF
L.D. 74
AN ACT TO UPDATE THE SYSTEM OF LEARNING RESULTS REVIEW TIMELINE
February 27, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan Murphy and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee. I am Eileen King, deputy executive director for Maine School Management Association, testifying on behalf of the legislative committees of the Maine School Boards Association and Maine School Superintendents Association in support of L.D. 74. This proposed change to transition the review cycle of Maine's content standards and performance indicators from a five-year to a seven-year cycle reflects a thoughtful and necessary adjustment to ensure a more effective and sustainable approach to curriculum review and implementation.
The Learning Results system plays a critical role in maintaining high academic standards for Maine's students, ensuring that our curriculum remains relevant, rigorous, and aligned with the needs of an evolving world. However, a five-year review cycle places significant demands on educators, administrators, and policymakers, often requiring frequent changes that can be disruptive to instruction, resource allocation, and long-term planning. Extending the review cycle to seven years will allow for a more deliberate, researchbased approach to curriculum updates, giving schools the time needed to fully implement and assess the impact of changes before undertaking another revision.
By adopting a seven-year cycle, Maine will align itself with best practices in curriculum development, providing greater stability for schools while maintaining the integrity of our educational standards. I urge the committee to support this bill to promote a balanced and effective approach to curriculum review and implementation.

Steven W. Bailey
MSBA Executive Director

Eileen E. King
MSSA Executive Director

Testimony
In Support Of
LD 74: An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline
Mallory Cook, Training and Early Educator Engagement Director, Maine Education
Association
Before the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee
February 27, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and other members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee,
My name is Mallory Cook, and I have the pleasure of serving the nearly 24,000 members of the Maine Education Association as the Director of Training and Early Educator Engagement. I am here today to testify in support of LD 74: An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline.
When we stood before you last session, we expressed concerns about implementing the proposed social studies standards due to the disruptions caused by COVID-19, the short review timeline, and the volume of recommended changes. As you may know, districts are not obligated to adopt the updated standards upon publication. Consequently, if following best practices, districts are likely not using the most recent revised standards in their respective content areas, as they have not yet had the time to develop action plans around these standards.
To illustrate this, before my work at MEA, I had the pleasure of working at the Hermon School Department. In this role, each department spent years collaborating with the Great Schools Partnership to derive performance indicators from the content standards, develop common rubrics and scoring criteria in student and stakeholder-friendly language, and create common formative and summative assessments. We refined these assessments to ensure they measured the intended indicators and standards. Only then did we begin working with grade-level teams to refine our unit planning, considering how our daily learning experiences would be sequenced, paced, and differentiated to meet our end goals. This process took years.
After implementing a unit, the Great Schools Partnership provided assessment refinement tools, unit refinement tools, and other resources that grade-level or departmental teams could use to reflect on student engagement and formative and summative assessment data. These tools

enabled us to adjust for the next time we implemented the instructional tools. For those who have taught, it is rarely the first or second time that a lesson or unit is best executed; it is almost always after the third time. Each subsequent semester or year, the tools are refined and improved, enhancing the student experience.
Extending the standards review period supports practices like these, promoting stability and consistency within schools. This allows instructors and students to adapt to the standards without worrying about significant changes disrupting their process.
A longer review cycle will provide districts with more opportunities to invest in and offer professional learning for educators who may face new requirements due to adopted changes. The most recent proposed social studies standards introduced significant content changes. Our primary concern is ensuring that educators receive the necessary professional learning supports to implement these changes effectively. Reflecting on my experience in Hermon, integrating such changes into our established standards, performance indicators, assessments, and units would have taken years, and this does not account for the extensive training our teachers would have needed to incorporate the new content and skills into the curriculum with fidelity.
Finally, we hope that a longer review cycle will encourage more public comments from key stakeholders when the review process begins. As more districts implement the current standards and make data-driven improvements based on student outcomes, we anticipate increased participation in these discussions. This will allow stakeholders to share insights on necessary improvements and aspects of the standards that should be maintained. Such engagement will ensure the steering committee has a comprehensive understanding of how the standards are being implemented across the state.
Thank you for your time and I'm happy to answer any questions you may have.

Good moming Representative Murphy, Senator Rafferty and fellow members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs. My name is Michael Brennan, and I
represent House District 115, which includes a portion of Portland.
Today I am here to introduce a bill for the Department of Education, LD 74, An Act to Update
the System of Learning Results Review Timeline.
This bill amends Title 20-A, �6209 directing the Department of Education to review the content standards and performance indicators in the Maine Learning Results. Currently, this review occurs on a 5-year cycle. This bill proposes that beginning in the 2025-2026 school year, the
reviews occur on a 7-year cycle. This recommendation supports what we have heard from educators in the field who have asked for more time to implement changes from these review
cycles.
The Department of Education will present testimony on this bill, and I respectfully request that you defer any specific questions regarding the content to them. I look forward to working with
you as the Committee deliberates LD 74.
Thank you for your consideration.
